stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple’s price slipped 0.8% on the day and remains 3.2% below its 52‑week high, still 35.2% above its low, reflecting modest pullback after a strong YTD gain of 22.2%. The stock is trading near the top of its range, so investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance and any macro‑tech demand shifts.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft is flat today, sitting 4.6% under its 52‑week high and 45.6% above its low after a 9.1% YTD rise. With the stock near the upper end of its range, the next catalyst is the Q4 earnings beat and cloud‑spending trends.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: Nvidia rose 1.1% and is now just 1.8% shy of its 52‑week peak, still 40.1% above its low after a 22.5% YTD climb. Investors should focus on AI‑related demand and the upcoming earnings release for forward momentum.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet fell 1.7% and is 15.9% below its 52‑week high, though still 43.3% above its low, with YTD growth of 7.5%. The key watch is ad‑revenue recovery and any impact from AI product rollouts.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon slipped 0.4% and remains 12.6% under its 52‑week high, 24.9% above its low after a 9.6% YTD rise. Attention should turn to retail traffic trends and the upcoming earnings commentary on margin pressure.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta edged up 0.1% but stays 6.6% below its 52‑week high, 38.3% above its low, after a solid 11.9% YTD gain. Investors should monitor user growth metrics and the rollout of AI features in its platforms.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla dipped 0.2% and is 27.7% off its 52‑week high, though only 18.7% above its low, with a YTD decline of 19.2%. The next inflection point is production updates and demand trends for its new models.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom fell 2.1% and is 28.4% below its 52‑week high, just 17.5% above its low, with a flat YTD performance. Watch the semiconductor cycle and any guidance on its data‑center and networking segments.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD rose 0.6% and sits 2.4% under its 52‑week high, still 273.9% above its low after a spectacular 175.5% YTD surge. The critical focus is whether the recent earnings can sustain momentum amid competitive pressure.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has rallied modestly today (+0.6%) but remains 55.5% below its 52‑week high, trading near the lower end of its range. The stock is still 20.1% above its 52‑week low, suggesting limited upside unless earnings or cloud guidance improve. Watch upcoming quarterly results for any shift in growth narrative.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce posted a solid daily gain (+3.1%) while sitting 10.5% shy of its 52‑week high and well above its low, indicating a mid‑range position. The recent pullback of 8.1% over the month leaves room for a bounce if the company delivers on AI‑driven revenue targets. Investor focus should be on the next earnings release and AI product adoption metrics.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan edged higher today (+0.7%) and is trading 8.8% below its 52‑week peak, comfortably above its low. With a modest YTD gain of 3.8%, the stock is holding steady amid mixed banking sector sentiment. Key watch point is the upcoming Fed policy outlook and JPM’s loan‑loss provisions guidance.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America slipped 1.3% on the day and remains 16.7% under its 52‑week high, though still 16.2% above its low. The broader banking weakness is reflected in its 12.9% monthly decline. Investors should monitor credit‑quality trends and any changes in net interest margin expectations.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa is barely up today (+0.1%) and sits 6.3% below its 52‑week high, with a healthy 22.2% cushion above its low. The modest YTD gain of 4.5% reflects steady transaction volume despite recent volatility. Watch for quarterly payment‑volume growth and any shifts in consumer spending patterns.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard dipped slightly (-0.3%) and is 8.3% under its 52‑week high, still 16.8% above its low. The YTD decline of 1.9% follows a broader slowdown in discretionary spending. The next earnings report and updates on cross‑border transaction trends will be pivotal.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix fell 2.5% on the day and remains 45.3% below its 52‑week high, barely above its low point. A steep 16% monthly drop and a 25.4% YTD decline underscore subscriber growth concerns. Investors should focus on upcoming subscriber guidance and any new pricing or content strategy announcements.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly slipped 0.6% but is only 10.2% under its 52‑week high, maintaining a strong position 44.7% above its low. The modest YTD rise of 6.9% reflects steady demand for its portfolio. Watch upcoming FDA decisions and pipeline updates for growth catalysts.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth edged down 0.5% and sits 15.8% below its 52‑week high, still 42.7% above its low, with a solid 10.7% YTD gain. The stock’s resilience hinges on enrollment trends and cost‑containment measures. Key focus will be the next earnings beat and any policy changes affecting Medicare Advantage.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has slipped 2.3% today and is down 4.6% over the month, sitting 7.1% below its 52‑week high but still 42.2% above its 52‑week low. The recent pullback follows a strong YTD gain of 26.8%, suggesting profit‑taking after the rally. Watch upcoming earnings guidance and any updates on its pharmaceutical pipeline for direction.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart is marginally up 0.3% on the day but remains 22.1% below its 52‑week peak, trading just 4.5% above its 52‑week low. The stock has underperformed YTD, down 6.9%, as consumer spending pressures linger. Investors should focus on same‑store sales trends and any shifts in discretionary spending forecasts.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco rose 0.5% today, trading 16.3% under its 52‑week high and 8.1% above its low, with a modest 7.5% YTD gain. The modest monthly dip reflects a broader retail rotation, but membership renewal rates remain a key catalyst. Watch the upcoming quarterly membership and sales growth numbers for momentum cues.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot fell 0.7% and is now 26.5% below its 52‑week high, essentially at its 52‑week low after an 11% monthly decline and a 16.5% YTD drop. The steep pullback follows weaker housing market data. The next driver will be the housing starts report and any signs of a rebound in DIY spending.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil edged up 0.7%, sitting just 3.2% shy of its 52‑week high while remaining 52.4% above its low, and has posted a robust 36.2% YTD gain. The modest daily rise follows a broadly stable energy price environment. Key focus will be the upcoming earnings beat expectations and crude price outlook.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola is flat today, trading 5.8% below its 52‑week high and 33.7% above its low, with a strong 27% YTD rise. The stock’s recent dip mirrors broader consumer staple softness. Watch the company's pricing strategy and volume trends in its emerging markets segment.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney dropped 3.4% on the day, now 11.9% under its 52‑week high and 10.5% above its low, with an 8.7% YTD decline. The slide reflects ongoing challenges in streaming and theme‑park attendance. Investors should monitor the next earnings release and any updates on the Disney+ subscriber growth and park recovery.
